english: You are firm in dwelling, firm in womb, you are firm. Sit in the firm womb, rightly, delighting in the first banner of the ukhya. May the two Aśvins, the two adhvaryus, seat you here.

hindi: शुक्र और शुचि, ग्रीष्म की दोनों ऋतुएँ: तुम अग्नि के भीतर संयोजन हो। द्यावापृथिवी व्यवस्थित हों, जल और ओषधियाँ व्यवस्थित हों, अग्नियाँ व्यवस्थित हों; अलग-अलग ज्येष्ठता के लिए नमस्कार, समान व्रत वाले। जो अग्नियाँ समान मन वाली इन द्यावापृथिवी के बीच हैं; ग्रीष्म की दोनों ऋतुएँ, व्यवस्थित होती हुई, जैसे देव इन्द्र में प्रवेश करते हैं वैसे साथ-साथ प्रवेश करें। उस देवता के साथ अङ्गिरा के समान तुम दोनों दृढ़ होकर बैठो।
english: Śukra and Śuci, the two seasons of summer: you are the joining within Agni. May heaven and earth be ordered, may the waters, the plants, the fires be ordered, each separately; homage for seniority, of the same observance. The fires which, like-minded, are between these two, heaven and earth: the two seasons of summer, being ordered, let them enter together, as the gods enter Indra. With that deity, like Aṅgiras, sit firm, you two.
notes: kalpetām etc. are forms of √kḷp, rendered 'be ordered'; the sense is tentative. 'agner antaḥ śleṣo 'si' is rendered literally ('joining within Agni'). The grammatical subject of abhisaṃviśantu (dual seasons with a plural verb) is uncertain, and 'indram iva devāḥ' could also be read 'the gods, like Indra'. Śukra and Śuci are kept as names; the line does not state what they are. 'pṛthaṅ nama jyaiṣṭhyāya': pṛthak may go with the fires ('each separately', as in the English) or with namaḥ jyaiṣṭhyāya ('separately homage for seniority', as in the Hindi); the ambiguity is not resolved.

notes: 'cakṣur me urvyā vi bhāhi' is rendered 'shine widely for my eye'; the case role of cakṣuḥ is unclear. prāṇa, apāna, vyāna are rendered by their literal senses (breath, out-breath, diffused breath). dvipād and catuṣpād are left as 'two-footed' and 'four-footed' without saying what they refer to.

english: The head is the vayas, Prajāpati the metre; ruling power is the vayas, the mayanda the metre; the prop is the vayas, the overlord the metre. hindi: विश्वकर्मा तुम्हें अन्तरिक्ष की पीठ पर बिठाए, विशाल और विस्तृत तुम्हें। अन्तरिक्ष को थामो, अन्तरिक्ष को दृढ़ करो, अन्तरिक्ष को हानि न पहुँचाओ। सब प्राण के लिए, अपान के लिए, व्यान के लिए, उदान के लिए, प्रतिष्ठा के लिए, गति के लिए। वायु तुम्हारी रक्षा करे, महान कल्याण और अत्यन्त सुखद आवरण के साथ। उस देवता के साथ अङ्गिरा के समान दृढ़ होकर बैठो।
english: May Viśvakarman seat you on the back of the atmosphere, you who are spacious and broad. Hold the atmosphere, make the atmosphere firm, do not harm the atmosphere. For all breath, for out-breath, for diffused breath, for up-breath, for foundation, for movement. May Vāyu protect you, with great well-being and with most beneficial covering. With that deity, like Aṅgiras, sit firm.
notes: The second sentence of line a lists datives ('for breath ... for movement') without a verb in this unit. mahyā is taken as the feminine instrumental of mahī 'great' with svastyā; chardis is rendered 'covering'. Line a contains a half-verse break (|).

hindi: नभस् और नभस्य, वर्षा की दोनों ऋतुएँ: तुम अग्नि के भीतर संयोजन हो। द्यावापृथिवी व्यवस्थित हों, जल और ओषधियाँ व्यवस्थित हों, अग्नियाँ व्यवस्थित हों; अलग-अलग ज्येष्ठता के लिए नमस्कार, समान व्रत वाले। जो अग्नियाँ समान मन वाली इन द्यावापृथिवी के बीच हैं; वर्षा की दोनों ऋतुएँ, व्यवस्थित होती हुई, जैसे देव इन्द्र में प्रवेश करते हैं वैसे साथ-साथ प्रवेश करें। उस देवता के साथ अङ्गिरा के समान तुम दोनों दृढ़ होकर बैठो।
english: Nabhas and Nabhasya, the two seasons of the rains: you are the joining within Agni. May heaven and earth be ordered, may the waters, the plants, the fires be ordered, each separately; homage for seniority, of the same observance. The fires which, like-minded, are between these two, heaven and earth: the two seasons of the rains, being ordered, let them enter together, as the gods enter Indra. With that deity, like Aṅgiras, sit firm, you two.
notes: kalpetām etc. are forms of √kḷp, rendered 'be ordered'; the sense is tentative. 'agner antaḥ śleṣo 'si' is rendered literally ('joining within Agni'). The grammatical subject of abhisaṃviśantu (dual seasons with a plural verb) is uncertain, and 'indram iva devāḥ' could also be read 'the gods, like Indra'. Nabhas and Nabhasya are kept as names; the line does not state what they are. 'pṛthaṅ nama jyaiṣṭhyāya': pṛthak may go with the fires ('each separately', as in the English) or with namaḥ jyaiṣṭhyāya ('separately homage for seniority', as in the Hindi); the ambiguity is not resolved.

hindi: इष और ऊर्ज, शरद की दोनों ऋतुएँ: तुम अग्नि के भीतर संयोजन हो। द्यावापृथिवी व्यवस्थित हों, जल और ओषधियाँ व्यवस्थित हों, अग्नियाँ व्यवस्थित हों; अलग-अलग ज्येष्ठता के लिए नमस्कार, समान व्रत वाले। जो अग्नियाँ समान मन वाली इन द्यावापृथिवी के बीच हैं; शरद की दोनों ऋतुएँ, व्यवस्थित होती हुई, जैसे देव इन्द्र में प्रवेश करते हैं वैसे साथ-साथ प्रवेश करें। उस देवता के साथ अङ्गिरा के समान तुम दोनों दृढ़ होकर बैठो।
english: Iṣa and Ūrja, the two seasons of autumn: you are the joining within Agni. May heaven and earth be ordered, may the waters, the plants, the fires be ordered, each separately; homage for seniority, of the same observance. The fires which, like-minded, are between these two, heaven and earth: the two seasons of autumn, being ordered, let them enter together, as the gods enter Indra. With that deity, like Aṅgiras, sit firm, you two.
notes: kalpetām etc. are forms of √kḷp, rendered 'be ordered'; the sense is tentative. 'agner antaḥ śleṣo 'si' is rendered literally ('joining within Agni'). The grammatical subject of abhisaṃviśantu (dual seasons with a plural verb) is uncertain, and 'indram iva devāḥ' could also be read 'the gods, like Indra'. Iṣa and Ūrja are kept as names; the line does not state what they are. Line b has a double space after abhikalpamānā in the input. 'pṛthaṅ nama jyaiṣṭhyāya': pṛthak may go with the fires ('each separately', as in the English) or with namaḥ jyaiṣṭhyāya ('separately homage for seniority', as in the Hindi); the ambiguity is not resolved.

english: Āśu is the threefold (trivṛt); Bhānta is the fifteenfold; the sky is the seventeenfold; the support is the twenty-onefold. Vivarta is the forty-eightfold; the support (dhartra) is the catuṣṭoma.

hindi: तुम अग्नि का भाग हो, दीक्षा का आधिपत्य; ब्रह्म सुरक्षित है, त्रिवृत् स्तोम। तुम इन्द्र का भाग हो, विष्णु का आधिपत्य; क्षत्र सुरक्षित है, पञ्चदश स्तोम। तुम मनुष्यों को देखने वालों का भाग हो, धाता का आधिपत्य; जन्म सुरक्षित है, सप्तदश स्तोम। तुम मित्र का भाग हो, वरुण का आधिपत्य; द्यौ की वर्षा और वात सुरक्षित है, एकविंश स्तोम।
english: You are the portion of Agni, the overlordship of dīkṣā; brahma is secured, the threefold stoma. You are the portion of Indra, the overlordship of Viṣṇu; ruling power is secured, the fifteenfold stoma. You are the portion of the watchers of men, the overlordship of Dhātṛ; birth is secured, the seventeenfold stoma. You are the portion of Mitra, the overlordship of Varuṇa; the rain of heaven, the wind, is secured, the twenty-onefold stoma.
notes: spṛta (p.p. of √spṛ) is rendered 'secured' tentatively. 'divo vṛṣṭir vātaḥ spṛtaḥ' has two subjects and a singular participle; it is rendered literally. nṛcakṣasām is taken as 'of the watchers of men' without naming who they are.

hindi: तुम वसुओं का भाग हो, रुद्रों का आधिपत्य; चार पैर वाला सुरक्षित है, चतुर्विंश स्तोम। तुम आदित्यों का भाग हो, मरुतों का आधिपत्य; गर्भ सुरक्षित हैं, पञ्चविंश स्तोम। तुम अदिति के लिए भाग हो, पूषा का आधिपत्य; ओज सुरक्षित है, त्रिणव स्तोम। तुम देव सविता का भाग हो, बृहस्पति का आधिपत्य; मिली हुई दिशाएँ सुरक्षित हैं, चतुष्टोम स्तोम।
english: You are the portion of the Vasus, the overlordship of the Rudras; the four-footed is secured, the twenty-fourfold stoma. You are the portion of the Ādityas, the overlordship of the Maruts; the embryos are secured, the twenty-fivefold stoma. You are the portion for Aditi, the overlordship of Pūṣan; vigour is secured, the triṇava stoma. You are the portion of the god Savitṛ, the overlordship of Bṛhaspati; the joined directions are secured, the catuṣṭoma stoma.
notes: 'adityai' is dative: 'portion for Aditi' (the preceding stomo and the avagraha give stomo 'dityai). catuṣpād is left as 'the four-footed'. samīcīḥ is rendered 'joined'.

hindi: सह और सहस्य, हेमन्त की दोनों ऋतुएँ: तुम अग्नि के भीतर संयोजन हो। द्यावापृथिवी व्यवस्थित हों, जल और ओषधियाँ व्यवस्थित हों, अग्नियाँ व्यवस्थित हों; अलग-अलग ज्येष्ठता के लिए नमस्कार, समान व्रत वाले। जो अग्नियाँ समान मन वाली इन द्यावापृथिवी के बीच हैं; हेमन्त की दोनों ऋतुएँ, व्यवस्थित होती हुई, जैसे देव इन्द्र में प्रवेश करते हैं वैसे साथ-साथ प्रवेश करें। उस देवता के साथ अङ्गिरा के समान तुम दोनों दृढ़ होकर बैठो।
english: Saha and Sahasya, the two seasons of Hemanta: you are the joining within Agni. May heaven and earth be ordered, may the waters, the plants, the fires be ordered, each separately; homage for seniority, of the same observance. The fires which, like-minded, are between these two, heaven and earth: the two seasons of Hemanta, being ordered, let them enter together, as the gods enter Indra. With that deity, like Aṅgiras, sit firm, you two.
notes: kalpetām etc. are forms of √kḷp, rendered 'be ordered'; the sense is tentative. 'agner antaḥ śleṣo 'si' is rendered literally ('joining within Agni'). The grammatical subject of abhisaṃviśantu (dual seasons with a plural verb) is uncertain, and 'indram iva devāḥ' could also be read 'the gods, like Indra'. Saha and Sahasya are kept as names; the line does not state what they are. 'pṛthaṅ nama jyaiṣṭhyāya': pṛthak may go with the fires ('each separately', as in the English) or with namaḥ jyaiṣṭhyāya ('separately homage for seniority', as in the Hindi); the ambiguity is not resolved.
lines_deva: सह॑श्च सह॒स्य॒श्च हैम॑न्तिकावृ॒तू अ॒ग्नेर॑न्तः श्ले॒षो॒ऽसि॒ कल्पे॑तां॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी कल्प॑न्ता॒माप॒ ओष॑धय॒ः कल्प॑न्ताम॒ग्नय॒ः पृथ॒ङ्नम॒ ज्यैष्ठ्या॑य॒ सव्र॑ताः
ये अ॒ग्नय॒ः सम॑नसोऽन्त॒रा द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी इ॒मे। है॑मन्तिकावृ॒तू अ॑भि॒कल्प॑माना॒ इन्द्र॑मिव दे॒वा अ॑भि॒संवि॑शन्तु॒ तया॑ दे॒वत॑याऽङ्गिर॒स्वद् ध्रु॒वे सी॑दतम्

hindi: एक से उन्होंने स्तुति की; प्रजाएँ अधीयन्त; प्रजापति अधिपति थे। तीन से उन्होंने स्तुति की; ब्रह्म रचा गया; ब्रह्मणस्पति अधिपति थे। पाँच से उन्होंने स्तुति की; प्राणी रचे गए; प्राणियों के पति अधिपति थे। सात से उन्होंने स्तुति की; सात ऋषि रचे गए; धाता अधिपति थे।
english: With one they praised; the offspring adhīyanta; Prajāpati was the overlord. With three they praised; brahma was created; Brahmaṇaspati was the overlord. With five they praised; beings were created; the lord of beings was the overlord. With seven they praised; the seven sages were created; Dhātṛ was the overlord.
notes: adhīyanta is an obscure form (possibly passive of adhi-√dhā or adhi-√i) and is left untranslated. The feminine numerals (ekayā, tisṛbhiḥ ...) have no noun in the line; 'with one' etc. is left as printed. brahma is neuter (sacred power), not the priest.
lines_deva: एक॑यास्तुवत प्र॒जा अ॑धीयन्त प्र॒जाप॑ति॒रधि॑पतिरासीत् ति॒सृभि॑रस्तुवत॒ ब्रह्मा॑सृज्यत॒ ब्रह्म॑ण॒स्पति॒रधि॑पतिरासीत्  प॒ञ्चभि॑रस्तुवत भू॒तान्य॑सृज्यन्त भू॒तानां॒ पति॒रधि॑पतिरासीत् स॒प्तभि॑रस्तुवत सप्त ऋ॒षयो॑ऽसृज्यन्त धा॒ताऽधि॑पतिरासीत्

english: With nine they praised; the fathers were created; Aditi was the mistress. With eleven they praised; the seasons were created; the seasonal ones were the overlords. With thirteen they praised; the months were created; the year was the overlord. With fifteen they praised; ruling power was created; Indra was the overlord. With seventeen they praised; the domestic animals were created; Bṛhaspati was the overlord.
notes: The nasal sign '~' in āsa~s is the edition's mark for āsan + s-; it is not a typo. ārtavāḥ is rendered 'the seasonal ones' (belonging to the seasons).

english: With nineteen they praised; the Śūdra and the Ārya were created; day and night were the two mistresses. With twenty-one they praised; the one-hooved animals were created; Varuṇa was the overlord. With twenty-three they praised; small animals were created; Pūṣan was the overlord. With twenty-five they praised; the animals of the wilderness were created; Vāyu was the overlord. With twenty-seven they praised; heaven and earth went apart; the Vasus, the Rudras and the Ādityas followed, going apart; they alone were the overlords.
